corpus.label: J. S. Bach, BWV 846
corpus.reason: Keyboard polyphony, cross-staff/voice timing, ties and fermatas.

corpus.label: C. P. E. Bach, H. 186
corpus.reason: Dense keyboard ornamentation: turns, inverted mordents, grace notes, staccatissimo and tenuto.

corpus.label: Joplin, Maple Leaf Rag
corpus.reason: Syncopated keyboard chords, multiple voices, repeat traversal and ties.

corpus.label: Schoenberg, Op. 19 No. 2
corpus.reason: Short modern keyboard texture with staccato, tenuto, accents and dynamic wedges.

corpus.label: R. Schumann, Op. 48 No. 2
corpus.reason: Voice/piano separation, sustain pedal, fermatas and expressive markings.

corpus.label: Weber, Clarinet Concertino reduction
corpus.reason: Large transposing wind-plus-piano score, multiple instrument IDs, ornaments and dynamics.

corpus.label: Beethoven, Op. 132
corpus.reason: Largest corpus file by written note-element count; entire quartet with repeats, long spans, grace notes and wedges.

corpus.label: Beethoven, Op. 133
corpus.reason: Second complexity axis: 12,970 note elements, 293 staccatos, 139 trills, 172 grace notes and a harmonic.

corpus.label: Mozart, K. 458 I
corpus.reason: Contrasting Classical quartet: repeat structure, staccato/slur compounds, trills and grace notes.

corpus.label: J. S. Bach, BWV 267
corpus.reason: Retains the independently audited 402-attack baseline and CLI example; four-part chorale, not an orchestral score.

corpus.label: J. S. Bach, BWV 29/8
corpus.reason: Detailed case study: three trumpets, timpani and SATB; inverted mordents, ties, fermatas and repeats. Authored MIDI programs are piano placeholders.

corpus.label: J. S. Bach, BWV 248/64
corpus.reason: Broadest selected instrumentation: 14 parts with brass, winds, strings, voices and continuo; routing and sustained ties.

obligations.mapping: 106 catalog coordinates; independently specified JSON; five release cases; field vectors
obligations.granular: six Berlin refinement cases, hash-bound token dictionary, PE schema/chunks
obligations.inverse: external clips, stale source, controller/note ordering and canonical re-encoding
obligations.wire: independent byte vectors, truncation/reserved bits, scaling, header ordering
obligations.piano: M2-126 ID and 31-byte details, ten literal dynamic centers and 22 inverse boundaries, key velocity and physical positions, natural decay and silent key actions
obligations.interpretation: nine instrument columns × 106 named sounds; authored shortening counterexamples; unknown scoped remarks; harmonic pitch-role and ornament-start counterexamples
obligations.profiles: 14 family cases plus discovery, state, details, timeout, invalidation, fallback and PE cases
obligations.cli: process-level Bach conversion to all three formats; independent XSD and overwrite checks
obligations.accounting: counted elements/attributes with dispositions; exact encoded magnitudes; rounding bound case
